opening_paragraphs: Suggestions or feedback?

Mechanical engineers developed a flexible sheet that digitally reconstructs its own shape as it moves. The material could be used as a wearable, motion-monitoring “skin” for physical therapy, virtual reality, and gaming.

Robert E. Hall PhD ’67 and Michael Woodford PhD ’83 share this year’s Nobel prize in economics. The two MIT alumni were honored for work that illuminates how government policy can spur growth in response to economic downturns.

Addressing a national need, the MIT for America initiative ranges across STEM fields and will engage students from kindergarten through community college, preparing them to live and work in a world increasingly shaped by science and technology.

The startup Encora Therapeutics began as a project in 2.009, MIT’s iconic product-design class, to help people with Parkinson's disease. Now, nine years later, the FDA has cleared Encora’s device to help adults with essential tremor.

Researchers developed a noninvasive way to identify senescent cells — which are still alive but have stopped dividing — within aging tissue. The advance could help diagnose age-related disorders and guide scientists working on new treatments.
This fact sheet offers a high-level summary of the many steps MIT leaders have taken to support our vibrant Jewish community.

MIT’s vital research and education — on topics such as human health, energy innovation, quantum computing, and advanced manufacturing — continue to advance national security, economic competitiveness, and quality of life for all Americans.

See More Results Suggestions or feedback? Home About MIT About MIT The MIT community is driven by a shared purpose: to make a better world through education , research , and innovation . We are fun and quirky, inventive and artistic, obsessed with numbers, and welcoming to talented people regardless of where they come from. Founded to accelerate the nation’s industrial revolution, MIT is profoundly American. With ingenuity and drive, our graduates have invented fundamental technologies, launched new industries, and created millions of American jobs. At the same time, and without the slightest sense of contradiction, MIT is profoundly global . Our community gains tremendous strength as a magnet for talent from around the world. Through teaching, research, and innovation, MIT’s exceptional community pursues its mission of service to the nation and the world . Home Admissions + Aid Admissions + Aid Intensely curious and driven to explore, the people of MIT value rigorous analytical thinking, ingenuity, hands-on problem solving, and big new ideas. Stimulating, supportive, and playful, the MIT community becomes, for many students, a second home. In our undergraduate, graduate, and professional admissions, we seek applicants whose strengths, interests, and values are a good match for MIT. Because the Institute is built on the idea that talent and good ideas can come from anywhere, we are a remarkable community, drawing students from all 50 states and from 137 countries. Many are members of the first generation in their family to have the opportunity for higher education. Above all, our students learn not to be afraid of hard problems, making their MIT education a springboard for many careers — and practical preparation for life. Intensely curious and driven to explore, the people of MIT value rigorous analytical thinking, ingenuity, hands-on problem solving, and big new ideas. Stimulating, supportive, and playful, the MIT community becomes, for many students, a second home.

In our undergraduate, graduate, and professional admissions, we seek applicants whose strengths, interests, and values are a good match for MIT. Because the Institute is built on the idea that talent and good ideas can come from anywhere, we are a remarkable community, drawing students from all 50 states and from 137 countries. Many are members of the first generation in their family to have the opportunity for higher education. Above all, our students learn not to be afraid of hard problems, making their MIT education a springboard for many careers — and practical preparation for life.

All prospective undergraduate students apply through the Office of Undergraduate Admissions, regardless of their intended program of study. On the undergraduate admissions site, you can learn more about our application process and read student blogs about life at MIT.
To pursue graduate study at MIT, you need to apply to one of our departmental programs. Each department has its own application website and admissions requirements.

For professionals in the workforce and for learners anywhere eager for MIT content without the full-time commitment of a traditional degree program, we offer a range of educational options — some online, some on campus, and some a blend of both.

All prospective undergraduate students apply through the Office of Undergraduate Admissions , regardless of their intended program of study. On the undergraduate admissions site, you can learn more about our application process and read student blogs about life at MIT. To pursue graduate study at MIT, you need to apply to one of our departmental programs . Each department has its own application website and admissions requirements. For professionals in the workforce and for learners anywhere eager for MIT content without the full-time commitment of a traditional degree program, we offer a range of educational options — some online , some on campus, and some a blend of both.
